title: Rational finite free models of integral continuous sheaves on strata
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a noetherian scheme. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] write $B_X=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/\varpi^n)_X$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and $E_X=B_X[1/\varpi]$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization]. Use module sheaves and sheaf tensor products [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Identify these rings with the continuous coefficient sheaves $C(-,A)$ and $C(-,E)$, respectively, using the quotient-projection and scalar-localization maps; for every locally closed immersion $h:S\to X$ identify $h^{-1}B_X$ with $B_S$ and $h^{-1}E_X$ with $E_S$ using continuous pullback [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction]. If $M$ is a $B_X$-module sheaf and $U$ a covering object of $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$, there is a natural comparison
$$h^{-1}(E_X\otimes_{B_X}M)|_U\cong(E_S\otimes_{B_S}h^{-1}M)|_U.$$
It is induced by the localization maps, is compatible with their units, and applies to any chosen pro-etale local model of $h^{-1}M$.

For an ordinary module $N$ over $A$, let $N_S$ denote its constant module sheaf over the constant ring sheaf $A^c_S$; for an $E$-module $V$ use $V_S$ over $E^c_S$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-sf-site-constant-module-functor]. In particular $B_S\otimes_A N$ denotes $B_S\otimes_{A^c_S}N_S$ [def-weil-pbc-continuous-constructible-module]. Suppose $N$ is finitely presented, meaning that it has an exact presentation $A^m\xrightarrow{D}A^n\to N\to0$ with $m,n$ finite [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. Put $V=E\otimes_A N$. There are natural isomorphisms of $E_S$-module sheaves
$$E_S\otimes_{B_S}(B_S\otimes_A N)\cong E_S\otimes_{A^c_S}N_S\cong E_S\otimes_{E^c_S}V_S,$$
whose maps on local pure tensors are $e\otimes(b\otimes n)\mapsto eb\otimes n$ and $e\otimes n\mapsto e\otimes(1\otimes n)$, respectively. No flatness or torsion-freeness of $N$ is assumed. These identifications commute with restriction to any covering object $U$.

More precisely, for every specified finite presentation as above, $V\cong\operatorname{coker}(D_E)$ and $E_S\otimes_{A^c_S}N_S\cong\operatorname{coker}(D_{E_S})$, where both matrices are obtained by the constant-section coefficient maps. If $P\in GL_n(E)$ and $Q\in GL_m(E)$ satisfy $PD_EQ=\operatorname{diag}(I_\rho,0)$, their constant-section matrices are inverse-preserving changes of basis over $E_S$ and identify these cokernels with $E^{n-\rho}$ and $E_S^{n-\rho}$, respectively, including $m=0$, $n=0$ and $n=\rho$.

Consequently, if on each stratum of a finite locally closed stratification of $X$ [def-constructible-stratification] the sheaf $M$ is pro-etale locally of the form $B_S\otimes_A N$ with $N$ finitely presented, then $E_X\otimes_{B_X}M$ is pro-etale locally finite free on those same strata, hence constructible in the rational sense of [def-weil-pbc-continuous-constructible-module]. Neither a global trivialization on a stratum nor a common rank on different covering objects is required.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2; paragraph before Definition 6.8.6; Definition 6.8.10 and Proposition 6.8.11(3); finite-presentation model calculation in the construction of Proposition 6.8.14(2).

proof.text: Use the canonical continuous coefficient pullbacks. Their naturality for A→E gives the square of coefficient maps. The inverse-image/scalar comparison, followed by scalar-tower reassociation on both sides of that square, gives the natural immersion comparison. On original pure tensors its four components give precisely the prescribed formula. Applying overFunctor gives the comparison on each specified slice.

The first scalar comparison is scalarExtensionTowerIso. Construct the second comparison by the universal property of scalar extension from constant modules: a tensor n maps to a tensor (1 tensor n). Its inverse uses the ordinary extension/restriction adjunction and multiplication by constant rational scalars. Generator extensionality proves both inverse identities and naturality. Apply overFunctor for slice statements. The generic comparison proof is extracted into ConstantScalarTowerComparison to meet the compile limit.

Apply scalarPresentationCokernel to the specified ordinary presentation. Its normalization holds on every original vector, and its projection equation identifies the rationalized module with the specified matrix cokernel.

Apply constantMatrixCokernelModels over the rational field to the preceding normalized ordinary quotient. Compose its rational-model cokernel identification with scalarModels. The scalar comparison normalization and the coefficient constant-unit equation give the required original integral-vector lifts. No flatness or injectivity is used.

For the supplied PDQ rank equation, rankNormalCokernel constructs the ordinary tail cokernel including all empty cases. Apply the coordinate-quotient transport in constantMatrixCokernelModels. It supplies row and column automorphisms, their specified inverse coordinates, and the sheaf tail formula. Compose the direct-model cokernel isomorphism with this tail isomorphism and apply overFunctor for each specified slice.

The rationalized ordinary finitely presented module is finite dimensional over E. Choose its finite basis using Module.finBasis, transport the resulting finite-free isomorphism through the rational realization functor, and compose with the scalar comparisons and the given local integral model. The scalarOverIso comparison retains exactly the specified covering object. This directly proves local finite freeness without invoking continuous matrix elimination.

Transport the rational continuous module to the lattice coefficient presentation by the explicit pointwise ULift ring isomorphism. The ring-restriction/pullback comparison identifies its restrictions with the above rational restrictions; the coefficient comparison under immersion is an isomorphism. Compare the two constant module sheafifications through their normalized ring units and transport scalar extension. Consequently a rational finite-power local model is the continuous coefficient model of the finite free ordinary E-module of the same rank.

Use the original finite locally closed stratification and original covers, with the finite-free ranks just obtained. Locally closed strata of a noetherian scheme are constructible. The finite free ordinary modules are finitely presented, so these witnesses prove the recorded rational constructibility predicate.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 6.8.2, Definitions 6.8.6 and 6.8.10, Proposition 6.8.14(2); explicit balanced scalar comparison, categorical cokernel transport, elementary rank-normal cokernel calculation, and a finite basis for the chosen local rational module. F8 completes the specified-presentation clause using ordinary scalar cokernels, exact rank-tail calculation and normalized constant-matrix cokernel transport.

Step checks:
- Step 1: lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction gives A_X ≅ lim(A/ϖ^n)_X, A_X[1/ϖ] ≅ E_X and h^{-1}A_X ≅ A_S, h^{-1}E_X ≅ E_S for locally closed h. Its noetherian hypothesis is present.
- Step 2: lem-pur-proetale-inverse-image-tensor-comparison(1) with O=B_X, F=E_X, G=M; the pure-tensor formula gives the unit compatibility. Slice restriction uses lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor.
- Steps 3–4: the balanced reassociations are checked through lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal. Step 4 applies lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-tensor to constant presheaves; the constant sheaf and constant module definitions are sheafifications, so it applies.
- Step 5: right exactness, plus the flatness-independent clauses of lem-sfb-constant-finite-free-presentation-extension (exactness, β_s, E_B(D)=D_B), plus finite-cokernel preservation. The flat clause is not used.
- Step 6: verified by hand. PD=JQ^{-1} kills relation tails, and v − P^{-1}(0,tail Pv) ∈ P^{-1} im J = im D. The cases m=0, n=0 and n=ρ are covered.
- Step 7: matrix elimination on the one-point space over the normed field E. Rank 0 and empty index sets are covered by its statement.
- Steps 8–9: def-weil-pbc-continuous-constructible-module with topological ring E; the witness is E_S ⊗ V with V ≅ E^{n-ρ}.

Edge cases: N=A/ϖ^a gives 0 rationally; N=0 and N=A^r behave as expected.

All eight off-unit citations are generic tool lemmas. They are listed in split_report.tool_uses, and I accept them.
